meta.title: Motorcycles, mopeds and quad bikes
meta.pdd: Rules: para. 2 (subparas 19, 50, 51), 9, 12 (subparas 12-14), 21, 22, 41, 47-48, 52, 63-69, 73-74, 76, 78, 80, 85, 101-107, 118, 126, 128-129, 134, 145, 156, 165, Annex 1 (signs 3.5, 3.20); List of Defects (paras 19, 37, 38.3, 43, 44); Road Traffic Act, arts 1, 57, 73-74; Examination Rules (paras 11, 16, 40); autodrome methodology for category A
meta.summary: You will learn what A1, A and B1 licences allow, and how to ride a motorcycle, moped and quad bike under the 2026 Rules (helmet, passengers, speed, position on the road, towing, lights), how to brake and take bends safely, and what awaits you at the test ground.

lesson.h: Categories A1, A and B1: what you may ride
p: Subcategory A1 covers light motorcycles, tricycles and quad bikes with a maximum design speed above 50 km/h, an internal combustion engine of no more than 125 cm³ and a power of no more than 11 kW, and all mopeds. Category A covers all motorcycles. Subcategory B1 covers tricycles and quad bikes ⟦17⟧.
An A1 licence is issued from age 16, and A and B1 from age 18. No driving experience is required for them ⟦18⟧.
list: A category A licence also confirms the right to drive A1 and B1 vehicles with a motorcycle-type seating position or motorcycle-type handlebars (art. 73(8))

From 5 April 2025 a category B licence also confirms the right to drive A1 and B1 vehicles (art. 73(8)). So with a category B licence you may ride a moped and a light motorcycle of up to 125 cm³ and 11 kW

Training at a training organisation is compulsory: you are admitted to the test only with a certificate of completion of the course, and self-study is not allowed (art. 74 of the Act, para. 6 of the Examination Rules)
lesson.tip: A 250 cm³ motorcycle is already category A, and category A is issued only from age 18.

lesson.h: Moped, motorcycle, quad bike: how the Rules tell them apart
p: A moped is a two- or three-wheeled motor vehicle with an internal combustion engine of up to 50 cm³ or with an electric motor, and a maximum design speed of no more than 50 km/h. Mokicks, scooters and similar vehicles are treated as mopeds ⟦19⟧. You may drive a moped from age 16 ⟦20⟧.

A motorcycle is a two-wheeled motor vehicle with or without a sidecar. Three- and four-wheeled vehicles with an unladen mass of no more than 400 kg, and scooters with a cylinder capacity above 50 cm³, are treated as motorcycles ⟦21⟧. So under the Rules a light quad bike follows the rules for motorcycles.

From 25 August 2026, motorised bicycles, electric or petrol, are treated as mopeds: they require registration with a number plate and a driving licence of at least subcategory A1, and they may not be ridden on pavements (Law of the Republic of Kazakhstan No. 326-VIII of 24.06.2026).
lesson.tip: A scooter of up to 50 cm³ is a moped; a scooter of more than 50 cm³ is a motorcycle.

p: A motorcycle or moped driver rides in a fastened motorcycle helmet and does not carry a passenger without a fastened motorcycle helmet ⟦22⟧. The passenger must also wear a fastened motorcycle helmet ⟦23⟧. An unfastened helmet flies off in a fall and does not protect the head.

A motorcycle may not be used if it lacks the safety bars, footrests and passenger cross handles provided by its design, if there is play in the joint between the motorcycle frame and the sidecar frame, or if the remaining tread depth of the tyres is less than 0.8 mm. A motorcycle with a sidecar must carry a first aid kit and a warning triangle ⟦24⟧.
list: Eye protection, gloves, sturdy footwear and clothing reduce injuries in a fall (UK Highway Code, rule 84)
Bright or fluorescent clothing by day and retroreflective items in the dark help other drivers to see you (same source, rules 86-87)
A passenger sits only in a seat provided by the motorcycle's design; people are not carried in the load body of a goods motorcycle ⟦25⟧
Children and teenagers under 16 are not carried on the back seat of a motorcycle or moped ⟦26⟧
A passenger in a state of intoxication is not carried on the back seat of a motorcycle or moped ⟦27⟧
A passenger does not stand on the footrests or the seat while the vehicle is moving ⟦28⟧
The passenger's helmet is fastened ⟦29⟧
lesson.tip: A passenger on the back seat: only from age 16, sober and in a fastened helmet.

lesson.h: What a motorcycle or moped driver may not do
p: In addition to the general prohibitions for all drivers ⟦30⟧, two-wheelers have their own:
list: Ride without holding the handlebars with at least one hand ⟦31⟧
Ride on one wheel or sit outside the place intended for the driver ⟦32⟧
Carry a load that projects more than 50 cm in length or width or hinders control ⟦33⟧
Tow with a motorcycle without a sidecar, or tow such a motorcycle; tow mopeds or tow with mopeds, except with a trailer designed for a moped ⟦34⟧
Enter a motorway on a moped ⟦35⟧

lesson.h: Lights by day and by night
p: In daylight, all moving vehicles switch on dipped headlights or daytime running lights ⟦36⟧. For a motorcycle this matters especially: its outline is narrow, and car drivers often fail to notice it.

In the dark and in poor visibility, a motorcycle and a moped switch on position lamps and a main-beam or dipped headlight ⟦37⟧. Main beam is switched to dipped in built-up areas on a lit road, when passing oncoming vehicles at least 150 m before the oncoming vehicle, and in other cases when others could be dazzled ⟦38⟧.

list: In a built-up area, no more than 60 km/h; in a residential zone and in residential courtyards, no more than 20 km/h ⟦39⟧

Outside built-up areas a motorcycle travels like a passenger car: on a road with a central reservation, up to 110 km/h; on other roads, up to 100 km/h; on a motorway, as sign 3.24 shows, but no more than 140 km/h ⟦40⟧
You must not exceed the maximum speed given in the vehicle's technical specification ⟦41⟧; for a moped it is no more than 50 km/h
Mopeds and other vehicles that cannot travel at 40 km/h may not enter a motorway ⟦42⟧

lesson.h: Where to ride on the carriageway
p: A motorcycle is a full road vehicle and occupies a lane like a car. If the carriageway is marked into lanes, you must keep strictly within them, and you may cross broken lines only when changing lanes ⟦43⟧. So riding between rows of cars along a marking line is an offence, even in a traffic jam. The Rules have no special provision for motorcycles riding in two rows: keep your following distance and lateral clearance like any driver ⟦44⟧.

Outside built-up areas, keep closer to the right edge and do not occupy the left lanes when the right ones are free ⟦45⟧. Vehicles travelling at no more than 40 km/h keep to the far right lane ⟦46⟧. Driving on shoulders, pavements and footpaths is prohibited ⟦47⟧.
A lane for route vehicles (sign 5.9) is for public transport (which the Rules treat as including taxis) and category M3 vehicles. A motorcycle may neither drive nor stop in it ⟦48⟧.
lesson.tip: A traffic jam does not give a motorcycle the right to ride between rows or on the shoulder.

list: Overtake on the left. On the right you overtake only a driver who has signalled a left turn and started the manoeuvre ⟦49⟧
The “No overtaking” sign (3.20) prohibits overtaking all vehicles except vehicles without a trailer that are travelling slower than 30 km/h (Annex 1). There are no exceptions for motorcycles
When you are being overtaken, do not accelerate and do not hinder the overtaking ⟦50⟧

You may drive on tram tracks running in the same direction on the left, at the same level as the carriageway, when all lanes are occupied, and also when driving around an obstacle, overtaking, turning left or making a U-turn, without hindering the tram. You may not drive onto tracks of the opposite direction ⟦51⟧

A left turn and a U-turn where there are such tracks are made from them, giving way to the tram ⟦52⟧. At an intersection a tram has priority over trackless vehicles if the traffic light allows all of them to move, and at an intersection of roads of equal status ⟦53⟧

p: On the carriageway vehicles are parked in one row parallel to the edge, but two-wheelers without a sidecar may be parked in two rows. At the edge of a pavement bordering the carriageway, only passenger cars, motorcycles, mopeds and bicycles may be parked, and only if they do not hinder pedestrians ⟦54⟧.
If you get off your motorcycle and wheel it beside you, you are a pedestrian under the Rules ⟦55⟧. This lets you, for example, wheel a motorcycle along the pavement to the entrance.

This advice is not from the Rules of Kazakhstan but from the New York State motorcyclists' manual (NYS Motorcycle Manual). The Rules require you to choose a speed and following distance that avoid a collision ⟦56⟧, and technique helps you do so.
list: The front brake provides at least three quarters of the total braking force. To stop, apply both brakes at the same time, but do not “grab” the front one
If the front wheel locks, release the front brake at once and then apply it again smoothly and firmly
Reduce speed before the bend. In the bend, look where you want to go
If you need to stop sharply in a bend, it is better to straighten the motorcycle first and then brake. If you have to brake while leaning, brake gently and roll off the throttle
Brake before or after a sharp swerve round an obstruction, but not during it

Slippery surfaces: road marking lines, metal plates and manhole covers in the rain, wet leaves, sand and gravel at the edge of the road. The first minutes of rain are especially dangerous, until the oil is washed off the asphalt
Cross rails, ruts and joints at an angle of at least 45 degrees
Keep a following distance of at least 2 seconds to the vehicle ahead

lesson.h: You are not seen: intersections and blind spots
p: More than half of collisions between motorcycles and cars happen when a car driver pulls into the motorcyclist's path: turns left in front of them or pulls out from a side road. Drivers often say they did not see the motorcycle (New York State motorcyclists' manual).
The priority rules for a motorcycle are the same as for a car (Chapter 13 of the Rules). But priority does not protect you from someone else's mistake.
list: As you approach an intersection, reduce speed and keep your fingers on the brake and clutch levers
Choose a position in the lane where drivers can see you better
Do not linger in the blind spot of a neighbouring car: it may change lanes without noticing you
If a car has stopped in the adjacent lane before an uncontrolled pedestrian crossing, continue only after making sure there are no pedestrians in front of it ⟦57⟧

lesson.h: The test for categories A, A1 and B1
p: The theory test has the same format for everyone: 40 questions, 40 minutes, and at least 32 correct answers are needed. If you open several categories at once, you take the theory test once and the practical test separately for each category ⟦58⟧.
The practical test for A and A1 is taken on a two-wheeled motorcycle, and for B1 on a tricycle or quad bike ⟦59⟧. For B1 the same test ground zones are provided as for category B ⟦60⟧.

For motorcycles, under the autodrome methodology (24pdd.kz, June 2026 edition, for Almaty), you perform the “Start”, “Dimensional corridor”, “Dimensional half-circle”, “Track board”, “Dimensional figure eight” and “Finish”. Touch the ground with a foot: 100 penalty points, that is, an immediate fail. Run a wheel over a control line: 25 points.
lesson.tip: Before the “Start” command: helmet fastened, mirrors adjusted, engine running, dipped headlight on.

keyFacts: A1 from age 16, A and B1 from age 18 ⟦1⟧
A1: motorcycles up to 125 cm³ and 11 kW, and mopeds; B1: tricycles and quad bikes ⟦2⟧
Since 05.04.2025 a category B licence also confirms the right to A1 and B1 (Road Traffic Act, art. 73(8))
Moped: up to 50 cm³ or an electric motor, and no faster than 50 km/h ⟦3⟧
Driver and passenger: in fastened motorcycle helmets ⟦4⟧
Under 16: not carried on the back seat of a motorcycle or moped ⟦5⟧
A load on a motorcycle projects no more than 50 cm in length or width ⟦6⟧
Motorcycle outside built-up areas: 100 km/h, 110 with a central reservation, on a motorway as the sign shows but no more than 140 ⟦7⟧
No towing with a motorcycle without a sidecar, no towing such a motorcycle, no towing mopeds or with mopeds ⟦9⟧
By day: dipped headlights or daytime running lights ⟦10⟧
Tread depth of motorcycle and moped tyres: at least 0.8 mm ⟦11⟧
mistakes: “A 12-year-old may ride on the back if he wears a helmet.” No: only from age 16 on the back seat of a motorcycle or moped ⟦12⟧.
“In a traffic jam a motorcycle may ride between the rows.” No: you drive strictly within lanes, and cross a broken line only when changing lanes ⟦13⟧.
“You do not need a licence for a moped.” Since 5 April 2025 you need subcategory A1, which a category A or B licence also covers ⟦14⟧.
“A motorcycle does not need lights by day.” Dipped headlights or daytime running lights are required for all moving vehicles ⟦15⟧.
“I can tow a friend on a moped with a rope.” Towing mopeds and towing with mopeds is prohibited ⟦16⟧.
“In a bend you can brake hard with the front brake.” Reduce speed before the bend, and for a hard stop straighten the motorcycle first (New York State motorcyclists' manual).
